context: Checkpoint 2026-08-03 (early). The farm-start fix produced a SECOND field bug and the anatomy is the lesson: extracting parseStartArgs removed two const declarations and left both references, so the operator got a ReferenceError from an already-published kit. node --check only parses, the follow-up grep searched the names the author remembered deleting, and the 200-test suite covers src/ — a bin is not importable. The extraction that made parsing testable left the bin LESS covered. farm-client is the only plain-JS package here, so the shared preset's no-undef (off, redundant under TypeScript) left the artifact that ships to a phone with no static check; it now lints, proven by reproducing the exact regression. parseStartArgs also grew statusRequested/cancelRequested, because asking for a flag and giving it a value are different questions — collapsing them would make `--cancel` without an id fall silently into the catalog listing. Kit republished 20:01 and its refusal paths exercised. Earlier: before-push now runs the three repo-wide gates (validate-packages, task:build-order:check, high-severity audit), each proven by breaking it on purpose; tidy.test.ts pinned a launch-directory-dependent spelling and now pins the rule; AGENTS.md §4 keeps only the invariant, the lane's own description carries the mutable.
